decisions.title: Leaf and branch domain separation
decisions.issue: Raw leaves, leaf digests, and branch digests can be confused unless their domains and input types are explicit.
interpretations: Hash raw leaves and branches without prefixes.
Use the RFC 9162 leaf and branch prefixes over distinct input types.
decisions.peer_behavior: transparency-dev/merkle v0.0.2 uses the RFC 9162 0x00 leaf and 0x01 branch domains.
decisions.selected_behavior: Both version-1 profiles hash RawLeaf values with the 0x00 prefix and branches with the 0x01 prefix over left and right digests; RawLeaf and Digest remain distinct types.
decisions.rationale: This preserves the RFC algorithm, second-preimage domain separation, and an API boundary that prevents accidental double hashing.
decisions.security_consequences: Leaf and branch substitution and accidental digest reuse fail at the commitment or type boundary.
decisions.resource_consequences: Per-leaf and cumulative byte limits apply before hashing; domain separation adds one prefix byte per hash invocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Unprefixed or pre-hashed trees are incompatible and must be rebuilt.
decisions.wire_consequences: Identical ordered raw leaves have RFC-compatible SHA-256 digests; package envelopes still carry package-owned identity metadata.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9162 defines both prefixes directly; no applicable erratum is currently recorded.
decisions.reconsider_when: RFC 9162 errata or a separately versioned profile changes the commitment scheme.

decisions.title: Empty-tree commitment
decisions.issue: Empty trees can be rejected, represented by a zero digest, or committed as the hash of an empty string.
interpretations: Use SHA-256 of the empty string as RFC 9162 defines.
decisions.peer_behavior: transparency-dev/merkle v0.0.2 commits the empty tree as SHA-256 of the empty string.
decisions.selected_behavior: Both version-1 profiles support an empty tree committed as SHA-256 of the empty string; decoders reject any other zero-size digest.
decisions.rationale: One RFC-compatible empty identity avoids zero-value and forged-empty ambiguity.
decisions.security_consequences: The invalid Go zero value cannot be confused with the canonical empty commitment.
decisions.resource_consequences: Empty construction retains no leaves or nodes.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Consumers using a zero digest or absent root must migrate to the RFC commitment.
decisions.wire_consequences: The root digest interoperates with RFC 9162 while the package binary envelope remains package-owned.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9162 defines the empty hash directly; no applicable erratum is currently recorded.
decisions.reconsider_when: RFC 9162 errata or a separately identified profile defines another empty commitment.

decisions.title: Ordered recursive tree shape
decisions.issue: Odd-width trees can duplicate, promote, pad, sort, or recursively split leaves and therefore produce incompatible roots.
interpretations: Pad to a power of two or sort leaves or pairs.
Split at the largest power of two smaller than the tree size.
decisions.peer_behavior: transparency-dev/merkle v0.0.2 preserves order and uses the RFC recursive largest-lower-power-of-two split.
decisions.selected_behavior: Preserve caller order and recursively split at the largest power of two smaller than the subtree size without sorting, duplication, promotion, or padding.
decisions.rationale: RFC 9162 uniquely defines this shape and authenticates order.
decisions.security_consequences: Caller order cannot be normalized away without changing the commitment.
decisions.resource_consequences: Depth and node work are bounded before recursion.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Duplicate-last, sorted-pair, promotion, and padding conventions are incompatible profiles.
decisions.wire_consequences: RFC-profile roots and proof paths match RFC 9162 for supported sizes.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9162 defines the recursive split algorithm; no applicable erratum is currently recorded.
decisions.reconsider_when: RFC 9162 errata or a new explicit profile defines another tree shape.

decisions.title: Complete root identity
decisions.issue: RFC 9162 tree algorithms do not define the complete package value identity needed to prevent cross-profile, cross-size, or cross-algorithm proof use.
interpretations: Bind profile, version, algorithm, size, and digest in an immutable value.
decisions.peer_behavior: Certificate Transparency interfaces commonly carry tree size beside the root hash but do not define this package envelope.
decisions.selected_behavior: Every Root binds profile ID, profile version, hash algorithm, tree size, and digest; verification and decoding reject partial or mismatched identities.
decisions.rationale: Interpretation metadata is part of the authentication claim and must not be implicit.
decisions.security_consequences: Complete binding prevents cross-profile, cross-size, and cross-algorithm proof substitution.
decisions.resource_consequences: Fixed-size metadata is validated before path allocation or hashing.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Consumers must preserve the complete Root rather than only digest bytes.
decisions.wire_consequences: Package binary formats encode identity metadata explicitly and are not Certificate Transparency wire formats.
decisions.upstream_status: The complete package identity is outside RFC 9162 and has no upstream erratum.
decisions.reconsider_when: A standardized envelope binds equivalent metadata with a compatible registry.

decisions.title: Inclusion proof path and verification
decisions.issue: Audit paths can be ordered differently or accepted with missing, surplus, or structurally impossible siblings.
interpretations: Store leaf-to-root nodes and accept any reconstructing path.
Require the unique RFC path for the bound index and size.
decisions.peer_behavior: transparency-dev/merkle v0.0.2 generates and verifies RFC 9162 leaf-to-root audit paths.
decisions.selected_behavior: Store siblings leaf-to-root and require the unique RFC audit-path length; reject missing, surplus, malformed, wrong-leaf, wrong-root, wrong-profile, and over-limit proofs.
decisions.rationale: A unique path and complete identity prevent malleable or context-free proof acceptance.
decisions.security_consequences: Verification binds every claim component and rejects surplus or structurally impossible input.
decisions.resource_consequences: Path count, bytes, depth, hashing work, and cancellation are checked before and during verification.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: RFC paths interoperate after adapting transport representation.
decisions.wire_consequences: Package binary proof encoding is not a Certificate Transparency wire format.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9162 defines generation and verification algorithms; no applicable erratum is currently recorded.
decisions.reconsider_when: RFC 9162 errata changes audit-path generation or verification semantics.

decisions.title: Consistency proof edge cases
decisions.issue: RFC 9162 defines nonempty strict-prefix proofs but omits zero-to-nonzero and equal-size API behavior.
interpretations: Accept any empty proof for equal sizes.
Require identical equal-size roots and reject the undefined zero-to-nonzero transition.
decisions.peer_behavior: transparency-dev/merkle v0.0.2 matches nonempty strict-prefix SUBPROOF nodes; the peer API does not define this package's equal-size identity policy.
decisions.selected_behavior: Equal sizes require identical complete roots and an empty proof; zero-to-nonzero generation, encoding, and verification are rejected; other proofs use RFC SUBPROOF order.
decisions.rationale: Undefined transitions must not acquire ad hoc trust semantics, while equal identity needs no path.
decisions.security_consequences: An equal-size digest mismatch cannot be hidden by an empty path.
decisions.resource_consequences: Proof node, byte, depth, and hash limits remain enforced.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Nonempty strict-prefix behavior matches RFC 9162; callers needing zero-to-nonzero policy must establish it separately.
decisions.wire_consequences: Undefined transitions have no package proof encoding; equal-size proofs encode an empty path bound to both roots.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9162 omits zero-to-nonzero and equal-size proof operations; no accepted erratum currently defines them.
decisions.reconsider_when: An accepted RFC erratum or successor specification defines either transition.

decisions.title: Multi-inclusion proof authority
decisions.issue: RFC 9162 defines single-leaf paths but no multi-inclusion proof representation, ordering, or duplicate policy.
interpretations: Canonicalize indexes and emit one minimal deterministic frontier.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained RFC 9162 peer defines a normative multi-inclusion proof representation.
decisions.selected_behavior: Copy, sort, and require unique in-range indexes, then emit the minimal left-to-right depth-first frontier; verification requires canonical leaf order and exact frontier consumption.
decisions.rationale: One deterministic minimal form prevents duplicate and ordering ambiguity without claiming RFC interoperability.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate, missing, reordered, and surplus claims fail closed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Selected leaves, indexes, frontier nodes, bytes, depth, work, and temporary memory are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: A future standard multi-proof needs a separately versioned profile.
decisions.wire_consequences: The frontier and binary encoding are package-owned even when the root uses the RFC profile.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9162 defines no multi-inclusion proof format.
decisions.reconsider_when: A suitable standard multi-proof format is adopted as a separately versioned profile.

decisions.title: Mutable builders and snapshot ownership
decisions.issue: RFC 9162 does not define mutable Go builder concurrency, failure atomicity, buffer ownership, or immutable snapshot behavior.
interpretations: Make every builder method internally concurrent.
Require caller synchronization while making operations atomic and snapshots independent.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained Merkle peers expose different ownership models, none of which is an RFC 9162 interoperability requirement.
decisions.selected_behavior: Builders are caller-synchronized; batches validate and compute before publication; inputs are copied or hashed immediately; returned snapshots own immutable state.
decisions.rationale: Explicit ownership and failure atomicity prevent partial commitments without hidden synchronization costs.
decisions.security_consequences: Failed work cannot publish partial commitments or retain hostile caller buffers.
decisions.resource_consequences: Preflight limits and cancellation bound temporary state; callers must prevent data races on mutable builders.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Successful incremental roots equal one-shot construction for every prefix.
decisions.wire_consequences: Concurrency and ownership do not alter Merkle commitments.
decisions.upstream_status: Builder ownership is package policy outside RFC 9162.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separate concurrency-safe builder can preserve atomicity, ownership, and existing commitments.

decisions.title: Canonical binary encoding
decisions.issue: RFC 9162 defines algorithms but no standalone package binary envelope for roots, proofs, or snapshots.
interpretations: Define a strict versioned envelope binding operation and complete identity.
decisions.peer_behavior: Certificate Transparency protocol structures are intentionally not reused or claimed by this package.
decisions.selected_behavior: Version 1 uses MTRE, explicit object type and identity, fixed-width big-endian integers, exact SHA-256 digests, and operation-specific canonical structure; decoders reject all non-canonical input.
decisions.rationale: A versioned typed envelope makes identity, allocation bounds, and compatibility explicit.
decisions.security_consequences: Type and identity binding prevent cross-operation substitution.
decisions.resource_consequences: Counts and size arithmetic are validated before allocation; parsing enforces byte, element, depth, work, memory, and cancellation limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Any incompatible layout requires a new encoding version.
decisions.wire_consequences: Encoded bytes are stable package wire contracts but are not RFC 9162 or Certificate Transparency wire artifacts.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 9162 defines no equivalent standalone envelope.
decisions.reconsider_when: A standardized envelope meets the same identity, canonicality, and fail-closed requirements.

decisions.title: Persisted snapshots and resume trust
decisions.issue: RFC 9162 does not define persisted tree topology, retained data, integrity validation, or trusted accounting for resume.
interpretations: Persist canonical digest nodes and independently validate every structural and cryptographic invariant.
decisions.peer_behavior: RFC 9162 peers do not define this package's snapshot persistence or resume policy.
decisions.selected_behavior: Persist canonical postorder digest nodes and metadata but never raw leaves; validate topology, hashes, root identity, uniqueness, and limits; ResumeBuilder requires a trusted expected raw-byte count.
decisions.rationale: Only authenticated and independently validated state may resume mutation, while unauthenticated accounting remains an explicit side input.
decisions.security_consequences: Corrupt, cyclic, shared, reordered, or oversized state fails closed before use.
decisions.resource_consequences: Raw application data is not retained and untrusted accounting metadata cannot silently control resumed limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Canonical snapshots round-trip and resume to roots identical to live construction.
decisions.wire_consequences: The trusted byte-count side input is required for resume and is not part of the Merkle commitment.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new commitment profile authenticates retained accounting metadata.
